title: Retry
subtitle: Non-blocking tiered retry topics to handle transient downstream failures without head-of-line blocking.
keyTakeaways: Sleeping inside a Kafka consumer poll loop blocks the entire partition (head-of-line blocking) and risks triggering a rebalance if `max.poll.interval.ms` expires.
Non-blocking retry architectures forward failed events to dedicated tiered delay topics (`retry-10s`, `retry-1m`, `retry-10m`).
Retry consumers inspect the message header's target retry timestamp and pause the partition until the backoff window elapses.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Because Kafka tracks progress using a single contiguous offset per partition rather than per-message acknowledgments, a consumer cannot simply skip offset 105, commit offset 106, and ask the broker to redeliver offset 105 later. If offset 105 fails due to a transient downstream HTTP 503 and the consumer performs a synchronous `sleep()` retry loop for 60 seconds, all 10,000 valid messages behind offset 105 in that partition suffer head-of-line blocking. Worse, if retries exceed `max.poll.interval.ms`, the consumer is kicked out of the group, causing the next consumer to re-read the exact same failing message.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: Sleeping inside a Kafka consumer poll loop blocks the entire partition (head-of-line blocking) and risks triggering a rebalance if `max.poll.interval.ms` expires.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Non-blocking retry architectures forward failed events to dedicated tiered delay topics (`retry-10s`, `retry-1m`, `retry-10m`).
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Retry:
bullets: **Blocking In-Place Retries (Within Main Consumer)**: Provides preserves strict per-partition ordering and requires zero extra topics. Best suited for Sub-second transient retries or pipelines where strict causal ordering cannot be relaxed.

**Tiered Non-Blocking Retry Topics (`retry-5s` -> `retry-1m`)**: Provides main topic never blocks; scales cleanly during partial downstream outages without rebalances. Best suited for High-throughput microservices calling external APIs, webhooks, or third-party payment gateways.
In-memory retries should be strictly limited to 1–2 fast attempts (e.g., 50ms–200ms) for brief network blips.
Longer backoff intervals (seconds to minutes) must be offloaded to dedicated **Retry Topics**.
Preserves full throughput on the main topic even when a subset of messages hits slow downstream dependencies.
Calling `consumer.pause()` stops fetching records while keeping the `poll()` heartbeat loop alive, preventing rebalance storms.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Retry across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Sub-second transient retries or pipelines where strict causal ordering cannot be relaxed, suited for environments requiring Preserves strict per-partition ordering and requires zero extra topics.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for High-throughput microservices calling external APIs, webhooks, or third-party payment gateways, where Main topic never blocks; scales cleanly during partial downstream outages without rebalances.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Popularized by Uber and standardized in frameworks like Spring Kafka (`@RetryableTopic`), the non-blocking retry pattern uses a cascade of fixed-delay topics (e.g., `orders-retry-5s`, `orders-retry-30s`, `orders-retry-5m`). Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Retry introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: causes severe head-of-line blocking for healthy keys; long sleeps trigger consumer group rebalances.

**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: relaxes ordering for the failed entity key (unless subsequent keys are also routed to retry); multiplies topic count.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Retry:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Retry consumers inspect the message header's target retry timestamp and pause the partition until the backoff window elapses.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Explain why a single shared retry topic with variable per-message delays doesn't work well in Kafka (a 10-minute delay message would block a 5-second delay message behind it), and why **fixed-delay tiered topics** solve this cleanly.
